findings.how_to_check: Inspect MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:199 to see the condition 'wom&has_dmonth&hasml' assigned to the spec titled 'Women, death month on profile: first name', or compare 'count if wom & has_dmonth' against 'count if wom & has_dmonth & hasml'.
findings.suggested_fix: In MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:199, change 'wom&has_dmonth&hasml|Women, death month on profile: first name' to 'wom&has_dmonth|Women, death month on profile: first name'.
findings.title: Baseline table 'Women, death month on profile: first name' condition erroneously restricted by hasml
findings.what_the_code_does: In MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:199, specification 5 in the spec loop is defined as 'wom&has_dmonth&hasml|Women, death month on profile: first name'. The condition includes '&hasml', restricting the sample to records where the model first name is non-empty after normalization, instead of using the unrestricted baseline condition 'wom&has_dmonth' matching its title and the check at lines 173-174.
findings.why_it_matters: The markdown table generated under '## Women, death month on profile: first name' will not report the baseline sample of women with a death month on profile (N = 23,365,543), but an undocumented subpopulation restricted to records with a model first name. It silently duplicates the restricted sample from specification 2 under an unrestricted heading, altering the sample size and all agreement and similarity metrics.

findings.how_to_check: In Stata, run 'count if wom & has_dmonth & hasml & cell==4' and 'sum xf_ml if wom & has_dmonth & hasml & cell==4' to confirm non-zero count and positive agreement in cell 4.
findings.suggested_fix: For the women's first-name table, either construct a first-name-specific cell classification where cell 4 reflects missingness of namefrst_ml alone, drop group 4 from the table when scoring hasml, or clarify in the header text that group 4 reflects missingness of either name in the full-name classification rather than missingness of the scored first name.
findings.title: Women's 'model first name present' table retains records in cell 4 and mislabels them as missing model transcriptions
findings.what_the_code_does: hasml for women requires only that the model produced a first name: 'gen byte hasml = (men & hm_f & hm_l) | (wom & hm_f)'. However, variable cell is imported from profile_names.dta, where cell==4 was defined using both names: 'replace cell = 4 if disc & !ml_ok', with 'ml_ok = namefrst_ml!="" & namelast_ml_ditto!=""'. Discordant women where the model produced a first name but no surname have hasml==1 and cell==4. When generating the table for 'wom&has_dmonth&hasml|Women, death month on profile, model first name present: first name', group 4 is tabulated, despite the markdown text stating that in model-names-present sections 'no source is scored on an empty model name; group 4 is then empty or near-empty' and 'group 4 (missing) refers to the model names alone'.
findings.why_it_matters: In the women's model-first-name-present table, group 4 is not empty or near-empty (containing over 500,000 records in the baseline population). These records have present model first names that are scored and achieve positive agreement/similarity in row 4, directly contradicting the text describing group 4 as representing missing model transcriptions.

findings.how_to_check: Count records where strtrim(namefrst_ml)!='' but cf_ml=='' to see how many non-fallback model names normalize to blank.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the fallback rule after pnorm so any model transcription that normalizes to empty falls back to Ancestry's normalized name, or align the raw string check exactly with the linkage tables, and document the behavior accurately.
findings.title: Fallback rule for 'Ours+Anc' does not match the linkage cleaning pipeline and fails to fall back on strings that normalize to empty
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 108-111 define fallback indicators fb_f = strtrim(namefrst_ml)=='' and fb_l = strtrim(namelast_ml_ditto)=='' on raw strings before normalization, and gen namefrst_mf = cond(fb_f, namefrst, namefrst_ml). The linkage pipeline in MATCHING/1_divide_and_clean_everyoneV5_women_addedV2.do:169-170 uses raw un-trimmed tests namefrst`name_type'=='' without strtrim. Additionally, strings consisting solely of punctuation, numbers, or titles (e.g. '.' or '(dr)') evaluate to false under strtrim()=='', preventing fallback to Ancestry, but normalize to empty under pnorm, receiving a 0 score in jwpair.
findings.why_it_matters: The markdown header claims 'Ours+Anc = ours with Ancestry's name wherever the model field is empty, field by field, as the linkage tables' New transcription'. In the presence of whitespace-only or punctuation-only transcriptions, the Ours+Anc metric does not exactly match the linkage tables' New transcription, nor does it replace uninformative model transcriptions with Ancestry's valid names.

structured_output.summary: The working tree additions cleanly integrate the new profile-name analysis into the replication preflight, input manifest, and driver. However, line 199 of MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do contains a critical syntax error where the baseline specification 'Women, death month on profile: first name' was given the condition 'wom&has_dmonth&hasml', erroneously restricting the baseline table to records with model first names. In addition, the 'model first name present' table for women retains observations in cell 4 whose first names were present and scored, contradicting table documentation describing group 4 as representing missing model names.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
